q:
Lena volunteers at an animal shelter and records information about each dog. She made a list of the information that is measured or counted with numbers.
1. Weight of each dog, in pounds
2. Age of each dog, in months
3. ?
Which information best completes Lena’s list?

choices.A: the number of walks each dog gets per day
choices.C: the color of each dog’s collar
choices.D: the name of each dog’s favorite toy

key: Answer: A. Weight and age are numbers. Only A is a number (a count of walks). B, C, and D are all categories (words), so the one choice that is different from the other three is the answer.
ref: Topic: Data Collection & Random Sampling · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 1/3 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #38 (reversed: the list is numbers, not categories)

q:
Use the pattern to help answer the question.
37 × 3 = 111
37 × 6 = 222
37 × 9 = 333
What is the value of 37 × 18?
key: Answer: B. 3 gives 111, 6 gives 222, 9 gives 333: the digit is how many 3s are in the number you multiply by. 18 = 3 × 6, so 37 × 18 = 666. A is just the next line after 333. D comes from 1 + 8 = 9.
ref: Topic: Numerical Patterns · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 6/14 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #18, new numbers

q: Which expression is equal to 60 − 3 × (8 + 2)?
key: Answer: A. The 3 multiplies both numbers inside: 3 × 8 and 3 × 2. Both are taken away, because the minus is in front of the whole group: 60 − 24 − 6 = 30. B multiplies only the 8. C changes the second minus to plus. D subtracts first.
ref: Topic: Order of Operations and Equivalence · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 2/11 · New problem · Built like: Lower 2 MA #26 and MA4 #8, with a minus in front of a + group (QR9 #27)

q: A baker has 96 cookies. She puts the same number of cookies into each of 8 boxes. If c represents the number of cookies in each box, which equation can be used to find c?
key: Answer: D. 8 boxes with c cookies each make 96 cookies: 8 × c = 96. That is the same as c = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. A is backwards, the mistake on Practice Test 6 MA #12.
ref: Topic: Matching Stories to Equations · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 1/6 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 MA #12

q: The number machine performs the same operation on each input to create an output. What is the output for an input of 30?
key: Answer: B. Inputs go up by 6 while outputs go up by 3, so the output grows half as fast: try input ÷ 2 + 3. Check: 4 ÷ 2 + 3 = 5, 22 ÷ 2 + 3 = 14. So 30 ÷ 2 + 3 = 18. A treats 30 as the next row (that would be 28). D is 30 + 3, leaving out the half.
ref: Topic: Input Output Tables · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 1/5 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 MA #13, rule a × input + b with a fraction

q: A store gave a 20% discount off the regular price of a jacket. The amount of the discount was $7. What was the regular price of the jacket?
key: Answer: C. $7 is 20% of the regular price. 20% = 0.2, so the price is 7 ÷ 0.2 = 35 (or: 20% is one fifth, so 7 × 5). A is 7 × 2. B is the sale price, 35 − 7.
ref: Topic: Percent Word Problems · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 11/33 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 MA #28

topic: Area and Perimeter of Complex Polygons
q: The perimeter of the whole figure is 27 centimeters. The perimeter of the square is 20 centimeters. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
key: Answer: B. The square’s side is 20 ÷ 4 = 5. The whole figure’s outline uses 3 sides of the square (15), so the triangle’s two outside sides are 27 − 15 = 12. The triangle also has the shared side, 5: 12 + 5 = 17. A leaves out the shared side. C is 27 − 5.
ref: Topic: Area and Perimeter of Complex Polygons · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 7/18 · New problem · Built like: Lower #1 #38

q: Nina did the problem 50 ÷ 12 × 182. Approximately what was her answer?
key: Answer: C. Work left to right: 50 ÷ 12 first. 48 ÷ 12 = 4, so 50 ÷ 12 is a little more than 4. 4 × 182 is about 730, and the exact answer is about 758: between 600 and 900. A comes from doing 12 × 182 first. Rounding 12 down to 10 and 182 to 180 gives exactly 900, which sits on the line between C and D, so that rounding is too rough here.
ref: Topic: Estimating Multiplication & Division · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 2/16 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #36, same two traps

topic: Remaining Amount after Reducing by Fractions
q: Tia had 12 apples and 9 oranges. She gave away 14 of her apples and 23 of her oranges. How many apples and oranges does she have left?
key: Answer: D. Apples: 1/4 of 12 is 3, so 9 are left. Oranges: 2/3 of 9 is 6, so 3 are left. 9 + 3 = 12. C is the number she gave away (3 + 6), and B mixes apples given with oranges left.
ref: Topic: Remaining Amount after Reducing by Fractions · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 5/10 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 MA #25 and MA4 #24

q: Garden A is a square with a perimeter of 36 feet. Garden B is a rectangle with a length of 12 feet. Garden B has the same perimeter as Garden A. Which statement correctly compares the two gardens?

choices.A: The area of Garden A is 9 square feet greater than the area of Garden B.
choices.B: The area of Garden B is 9 square feet greater than the area of Garden A.
choices.C: The two gardens have the same area because they have the same perimeter.
choices.D: The area of Garden A is 3 square feet greater than the area of Garden B.

key: Answer: A. Garden A: each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 ft, so the area is 9 × 9 = 81 square feet. Garden B: the two lengths use 12 + 12 = 24 ft, so the two widths share 36 − 24 = 12 ft, and each width is 6 ft. Its area is 12 × 6 = 72 square feet. 81 − 72 = 9, and Garden A is the bigger one. B has the right number in the wrong direction (her QR9 #30 slip). C thinks the same perimeter means the same area. D compares the sides (9 − 6), not the areas.
ref: Topic: Comparing Areas · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 2/3 · New problem · Built like: QR8 #32 and QR9 #30 (wrong both times, last third), now mixed with perimeter

q: Mia has a roll with 4 yards of ribbon and a box of 40 beads. She wants to make 15 bows. Each bow uses 10 inches of ribbon and 2 beads. There are 3 feet in 1 yard and 12 inches in 1 foot. Which statement best explains whether Mia has enough ribbon?

choices.A: Since 4 × 12 = 48 is less than 150, Mia does not have enough ribbon.
choices.B: Since 4 × 36 = 144 is less than 150, Mia does not have enough ribbon.
choices.C: Since 4 × 36 = 144 is less than 150, Mia does have enough ribbon.
choices.D: Since 40 beads is more than 15 × 2 = 30 beads, Mia does have enough ribbon.

key: Answer: B. 1 yard = 3 × 12 = 36 inches, so 4 yards = 144 inches. 15 bows need 15 × 10 = 150 inches. 144 is less than 150, so she does not have enough. A uses 12 inches in a yard. C has the right numbers and the wrong conclusion. D is about beads, which the question does not ask.
ref: Topic: English Unit Conversions · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 1/2 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #25, with more steps and extra information

q: P and Q are different digits from 1 through 9. What digit does P represent?
key: Answer: B. Work from the ones column. 9 − Q = 3, so Q = 6. Tens column: Q − P = 2, so 6 − P = 2 and P = 4. Hundreds column check: P − 3 = 4 − 3 = 1. So 469 − 346 = 123. No column needs a borrow. C is Q, not P. D adds 6 + 2 instead of subtracting.
ref: Topic: Cryptarithm / digit substitution · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 6/9 · New problem · Built like: QR8 #30 (her miss, last third), now with no borrow as the parent asked

q: Which list shows the fractions 47, 23, 59, and 35 ordered from greatest to least?

choices.A: 59,  47,  35,  23
choices.B: 23,  35,  59,  47
choices.C: 35,  23,  47,  59
choices.D: 23,  35,  47,  59

key: Answer: D. As decimals: 2/3 ≈ 0.667, 3/5 = 0.6, 4/7 ≈ 0.571, 5/9 ≈ 0.556. The close pair is 4/7 and 5/9: cross-multiply, 4 × 9 = 36 and 5 × 7 = 35, so 4/7 is bigger. A is least to greatest (bigger numbers do not mean a bigger fraction). B swaps the close pair. C swaps 2/3 and 3/5.
ref: Topic: Comparing & Ordering Fractions & Decimals · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 9/23 · New problem · Built like: QR8 #27, QR6 #32, QR2 #38 (her misses, last third)

q: Lisa ran 78 mile on Monday, 0.85 mile on Tuesday, and 45 mile on Wednesday. How much farther did she run on her longest day than on her shortest day?
key: Answer: C. 7/8 = 0.875 and 4/5 = 0.8. In order: 0.8, 0.85, 0.875. Longest minus shortest: 0.875 − 0.8 = 0.075. A is Monday minus Tuesday. B is Tuesday minus Wednesday. D is 1 − 0.875.
ref: Topic: Converting to a Decimal · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 8/37 · New problem · Built like: Lower #1 #29 (decimal word problem) and her order-three gap

q: The price of a bike is increased by 25%. The new price is then decreased by 20%. What is the overall percent increase or percent decrease from the original price?
key: Answer: A. Start with $100. 25% more is $125. 20% of 125 is 25, so the price goes back to $100: no change. B just subtracts 25 − 20, but the 20% is taken from the bigger new price.
ref: Topic: Percent Increase Decrease basic · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/4 · New problem · Built like: Lower #4 #38

q: Which statement is true?

choices.A: A rhombus is always a square.
choices.B: A rectangle is always a rhombus.
choices.C: A rhombus is always a rectangle.
choices.D: A square is always a rhombus.

key: Answer: D. A rhombus has 4 equal sides. A square has 4 equal sides (and 4 right angles), so every square is a rhombus. A rhombus does not need right angles, so A and C are false. A rectangle does not need equal sides, so B is false.
ref: Topic: Identifying Shapes · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 2/10 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 MA #23 and Lower 5 MA #28 (rhombus)

q: How many whole numbers between 41 and 91 have 6 as a factor?
key: Answer: C. "Has 6 as a factor" means the number can be divided by 6 with no remainder, so these are the multiples of 6. The first one after 41 is 42 = 6 × 7. The last one before 91 is 90 = 6 × 15. Count 7, 8, …, 15: that is 15 − 7 + 1 = 9 numbers. B is her shortcut (91 − 41) ÷ 6 = 8 R2, which misses one.
ref: Topic: Counting Multiples within a Range · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/9 · New problem · Built like: QR9 #36 and QR6 #28 (her misses, last third), new "factor" wording

q: The length of AD is x. The length of AB is 4. The length of BC is y. What is the length of CD?
key: Answer: D. CD is what is left of AD after taking away AB and BC: x − 4 − y. Check with numbers: if AD = 20 and BC = 9, then CD = 20 − 4 − 9 = 7. A adds y back (her QR9 #27 change). C takes the whole line away from the parts.
ref: Topic: Split Line Segments · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 3/5 · New problem · Built like: QR9 #27 and QR3 #37 (her misses, last third), new layout: the end piece is asked

q: Mila had □ stamps and then she gave ○ of them to Jon. Now, Jon has △ times as many stamps as Mila had. Which expression represents the number of stamps Jon had to begin with?
key: Answer: A. "As many as Mila HAD" means her starting number, □. So Jon now has △ × □. He got ○ from Mila, so before that he had △ × □ − ○. Try □ = 10, ○ = 2, △ = 3: Jon now has 30 and started with 28. D uses what Mila has left, which is a different question.
ref: Topic: Algebra with Geometric Shapes · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/5 · New problem · Built like: Lower #4 #35, same wording

q: The base of a triangle is 8 meters (m). Which statement correctly compares the value of A to the height of the triangle? (A = 12 × base × height)

choices.A: The value of A is always 4 times the value of the height.
choices.B: The value of A is always 12 the value of the height.
choices.C: The value of A is always 8 times the value of the height.
choices.D: The value of A can be the same as the value of the height.

key: Answer: A. Put the base into the formula: A = 1/2 × 8 × height = 4 × height. Check: height 3 gives A = 12, which is 4 times 3. B uses only the 1/2. C uses only the 8.
ref: Topic: Area of Triangles · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/16 · New problem · Built like: Lower 2 MA #30 and MA4 #17

topic: Remainder when Divided by a given Number
q: A soccer team needs to sell 300 raffle tickets. They have already sold 130 tickets. The 8 players will sell the rest, and each player will sell the same number of tickets. What is the fewest number of tickets each player must sell for the team to reach its goal?
key: Answer: B. Tickets still to sell: 300 − 130 = 170. 170 ÷ 8 = 21 R2. If each player sells 21, that is only 168, 2 short, so each must sell 22. A forgets the 2 left over. C and D divide the whole goal, 300 ÷ 8, and forget the 130 already sold (her QR6 #33 slip).
ref: Topic: Remainder when Divided by a given Number · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/7 · New problem · Built like: QR6 #33 (her miss, last third)

q: A pair of shoes cost $45. The price was decreased by 20%. Sam paid for the shoes at the new price with a $50 bill. How much change did Sam get?
key: Answer: C. 20% of 45 is 9, so the new price is 45 − 9 = $36. Change from $50: 50 − 36 = $14. A takes 0.20 off the price instead of 20% of it. B is the discount, D is the new price.
ref: Topic: Percent Increase Decrease basic · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/4 · New problem · Built like: QR9 #8 language (Lower 4 #38 wording)

key: Answer: C. There are 6 × 5 = 30 squares. 9 are white, so 21 are tiled. 21/30 = 7/10 = 70%. A reads the count 21 as a percent. B is the part with no tile.

q: A pet store has fish, birds, and hamsters. There are 2 times as many fish as birds and 4 times as many birds as hamsters. There are 65 of these animals in all. How many fish are there?
key: Answer: D. Hamsters = 1 part, birds = 4 parts, fish = 2 × 4 = 8 parts. 13 parts = 65, so 1 part = 5. Fish = 8 × 5 = 40. A is hamsters, C is birds, B is the number of parts.
ref: Topic: Word Problems with Ratios · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 6/12 · New problem · Built like: MA4 #27 and QR9 #32 (real drill gid 1140)

q: The figure shown may be folded along one or more of the dotted lines. Which line or lines, when folded, will make the two halves match exactly?

choices.C: both line p and line q
choices.D: line p, line q, and line r

key: Answer: B. Fold on q (up and down): the left and right halves match. Fold on p (across): the top half has a bump going out, but the bottom half has a dent going in, so they do not match. Line r is not a line of symmetry of a rectangle that is not a square.
ref: Topic: Shape Construction & Symmetry in 2-D Figures · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 1/2 · New problem · Built like: What to Expect #24

q: The table shows how a number machine changes each input number (△) into an output number (■). Which equation shows the rule for the number machine?
key: Answer: A. Check every row, not just the first one. B works only for 2. C works for 2 and 3 but gives 20 for 5. D works only for 6. A: 2 × 2 + 1 = 5, 3 × 3 + 1 = 10, 5 × 5 + 1 = 26, 6 × 6 + 1 = 37.
ref: Topic: Input Output Tables · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 1/5 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #6 (pick the rule) and Lower 5 MA (square rule)

q:
□ + □ + △ = 26
□ − △ = 4
What is the value of △?
key: Answer: B. The second line says □ is 4 more than △. Replace each □ in the first line with △ + 4: △ + 4 + △ + 4 + △ = 26, so three △ = 18 and △ = 6. Then □ = 10. C is □. D is 26 ÷ 2.
ref: Topic: Algebra with Geometric Shapes · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/5 · New problem · Built like: MA4 #5 and Lower 1 #37

q: Ana wants to cover a wall with rectangular tiles. The wall is 96 inches long and 60 inches high. Each tile is 8 inches long and 6 inches high. If she knows how to find the area of a rectangle, how can Ana find how many tiles she needs without putting them all on the wall? (A = l × w)
key: Answer: D. Along the length, 96 ÷ 8 = 12 tiles fit. Up the height, 60 ÷ 6 = 10 tiles fit. 12 × 10 = 120 tiles. B divides the length by the tile’s height, so the tiles are turned the wrong way.
ref: Topic: Matching Stories to Equations · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 1/6 · New problem · Built like: Lower 2 #32

topic: No Remainder when Divided by a given Number
q: Kofi and 8 other students each sold the same number of raffle tickets. Which number could be the total number of tickets the students sold?
key: Answer: A. Kofi and 8 others is 9 students, so the total must divide by 9: its digits add to a multiple of 9. 1 + 5 + 1 + 2 = 9, and 1,512 ÷ 9 = 168. D divides by 8, which comes from counting only 8 students. C divides by 3 but not 9.
ref: Topic: No Remainder when Divided by a given Number · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 6/16 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 MA #29 (and the digit-sum rule from Lower 1 MA #24)

q: Four students are collecting cans for a food bank. A grocery store promised that for every 2 cans the students collect, the store will add 1 more can. The table shows how many cans each student collected. How many cans will the food bank get in all from the students and the store?
key: Answer: C. The students collected 18 + 24 + 15 + 23 = 80 cans. The store adds 1 for every 2, so 80 ÷ 2 = 40 more. Total 80 + 40 = 120. B stops before the store’s part. D doubles, as if the store matched every can.
ref: Topic: Determining Total Cost · Diagram: yes · Wrong so far: 1/10 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 MA #30, a second format

topic: Finding Area/Perimeter of Rectangle, given Length & Width
q: The perimeter of a square is 32 centimeters. If a rectangle with a width of 4 centimeters has the same area as the square, what is the length of the rectangle in centimeters?
key: Answer: B. Square side: 32 ÷ 4 = 8, area 8 × 8 = 64. Rectangle: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 long. A stops at the square’s side, D at the area.
ref: Topic: Finding Area/Perimeter of Rectangle, given Length & Width · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 3/13 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 MA #30

q: A baker made □ muffins in the morning and ○ muffins in the afternoon. She puts △ muffins in each box. Which expression represents the number of boxes she fills with all the muffins?
key: Answer: A. All the muffins: □ + ○. Boxes: that total ÷ △. The parentheses matter: C divides only ○. Try 20 + 16 muffins, 6 per box: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 boxes.
ref: Topic: Translating Math Expressions · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 9/33 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 #33 and MA4 #28

q: A pack of 18 batteries costs $47. At the same price for each battery, about how much would 63 batteries cost?
key: Answer: C. One battery: 47 ÷ 18. 2 × 18 = 36 and 3 × 18 = 54, so it is about 2.6, not 2. 2.6 × 63 is about 164, between $150 and $200. B comes from dropping the 0.6 (2 × 63 = 126). A comes from 18 × 63 ÷ 47.
ref: Topic: Estimating Multiplication & Division · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 2/16 · New problem · Built like: Lower #6 #36, word-problem version

q:
Use the number pattern to answer the question.
3,  5,  9,  17,  33,  ...
What is the 7th number in the pattern?
key: Answer: C. Write the differences: 2, 4, 8, 16. Each difference doubles, so the next ones are 32 and 64. 6th: 33 + 32 = 65. 7th: 65 + 64 = 129. A stops at the 6th. B adds 32 again. D doubles the number 65 instead of the difference (the MA4 #25 slip).
ref: Topic: Numerical Patterns · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 6/14 · New problem · Built like: Lower 1 MA #21 and MA4 #25

q: A jar is filled with 50 marbles. Each marble takes up 2 cubic centimeters of space. There are gaps between the marbles in the jar. Which statement best describes the volume of the jar?

choices.A: The volume of the jar is exactly 50 cubic centimeters.
choices.B: The volume of the jar is exactly 100 cubic centimeters.
choices.C: The volume of the jar is less than 100 cubic centimeters.
choices.D: The volume of the jar is more than 100 cubic centimeters.

key: Answer: D. The marbles take up 50 × 2 = 100 cubic centimeters. The jar holds the marbles AND the gaps, so its volume is more than 100. B forgets the gaps.

q: A class has 32 students. 38 of the students walk to school. 14 of the remaining students ride bikes. The rest take the bus. How many students take the bus?
key: Answer: D. Walk: 3/8 of 32 = 12, so 20 remain. Bikes: 1/4 of 20 = 5. Bus: 20 − 5 = 15. B takes 1/4 of all 32 instead of the remaining students (8 bikes), and C is the bus count that follows from it (32 − 12 − 8). A is the bikes.
ref: Topic: Fractional Parts Word Problems · Diagram: no · Wrong so far: 1/8 · New problem · Built like: Lower 5 #33 step chain (fraction of the rest)

q: Use the diagram of the cube to answer the question. How many small cubes are being used to build the large cube?
key: Answer: C. Each edge is 5 small cubes: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. A counts one face. B counts the 3 faces you can see. D counts 6 faces.

q: Which phrase is represented by the expression 3 × (n − 4)?

choices.A: 3 times the difference of n and 4
choices.C: the difference of 4 and n, times 3
choices.D: 3 more than the difference of n and 4

key: Answer: A. The parentheses come first: the difference of n and 4 is n − 4, then 3 times it. B is 3 × n − 4, with no parentheses. C is 3 × (4 − n), in the wrong order.
